page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Combine over one denominator
steps.margin_note: One fraction, so the numerator can be worked on as a single expression.

recall.must_convey: That the two fractions are combined over the common denominator sin10° cos10°.
accept: put both over the common denominator sin ten cos ten
combine into a single fraction
take the common denominator first
common denominator teeskoni okate fraction ga rayali
combine the two terms over one denominator

steps.why: Nothing can be simplified while the expression is two separate fractions. Combining is what makes the numerator attackable.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the numerators without a common denominator.

steps.label: Take 2 out to make known angles
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the idea of the question. Taking 2 out turns the coefficients into 1/2 and √3/2 — which are sin 30° and cos 30°.

recall.must_convey: That 2 is factored out so the coefficients become 1/2 and √3/2, recognised as sin30° and cos30°.
accept: take two out so the coefficients become half and root three over two which are sin thirty and cos thirty
factor a two so the numbers turn into known trig values
half is sin thirty and root three by two is cos thirty
two common teeste half and root three by two vasthundi, avi sin thirty cos thirty
recognise the coefficients as thirty degree values

steps.why: A stray √3 almost always signals a 30° or 60° angle in disguise. Spotting that is what turns a messy numerator into a single sine.
common_mistakes: Failing to take the 2 out and never seeing the known values.
Matching 1/2 to cos 30° instead of sin 30°.

steps.label: Apply sin(A−B)
steps.margin_note: sinA cosB − cosA sinB is sin(A−B), so the whole numerator collapses to 2 sin20°.

recall.must_convey: That sinA cosB − cosA sinB = sin(A−B) is applied, giving 2 sin20°.
accept: use sin A cos B minus cos A sin B equals sin A minus B to get two sin twenty
the numerator collapses to two sin twenty degrees
apply the compound angle formula
sin A minus B formula tho two sin twenty vasthundi
the top becomes two sin twenty

steps.why: The numerator was built to match that formula exactly — which is why the 2 had to come out first.
common_mistakes: Getting the order backwards as sin(10° − 30°).

steps.label: Expand sin20° and cancel
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sin20° is 2 sin10° cos10°, which is exactly the denominator — so everything cancels and only the numbers survive.

recall.must_convey: That sin20° = 2 sin10° cos10°, which cancels the denominator entirely and leaves 4.
accept: sin twenty is two sin ten cos ten which cancels the denominator leaving four
expand sin twenty and everything cancels to give four
the denominator cancels and the answer is four
sin twenty ni two sin ten cos ten ga rasthe anni cancel ayi four vasthundi
after cancelling only four is left

steps.why: The answer is a whole number because the denominator was always a disguised copy of the numerator. Every step was arranging for that cancellation.
common_mistakes: Getting 2 instead of 4 by dropping one of the twos.
